title: LS-MDRM State Dictionary
description: Defines the full state model S_n = S_n^core + S_n^diag, scoring rules, and construct semantics.

state_n.description: Transition index n, starting at 0 for the initial state.

core.description: S_n^core = [P, G, C, F, R]_n — anchored ordinal scoring. Do not collapse into a single quality score.

P.description: Recursive linkage. Degree to which the current state traces back to predecessor states through legitimate ancestry chains.

scoring_levels.1: Weak linkage; predecessor referenced but ancestry chain not established.
scoring_levels.2: Partial linkage; predecessor established but transformation rule absent or weak.
scoring_levels.3: Strong linkage; predecessor established and transformation rule present.
scoring_levels.4: Full recursive linkage; complete ancestry chain with transformation rule and evidence binding.

G.description: Empirical grounding. Degree to which claims in the current state are supported by admissible evidence.

scoring_levels.1: Evidence cited but not bound to corpus version or location.
scoring_levels.2: Evidence bound to corpus version; location not exact.
scoring_levels.3: Evidence bound to exact location and corpus version.
scoring_levels.4: Evidence bound to exact location, corpus version, and transformation rule; counterevidence acknowledged.

C.description: Causal novelty. Degree to which the transition introduces a non-trivially new causal or inferential step not present in predecessors.

scoring_levels.0: Restatement or paraphrase; no new causal content.
scoring_levels.2: Partial novelty; some new causal element but significant overlap with predecessor.
scoring_levels.3: Substantial novelty; new causal element clearly distinct from predecessor.
scoring_levels.4: Full causal novelty; new inferential step with no predecessor overlap.

F.description: Discriminability / falsifiability. Degree to which the current state makes claims that can be distinguished from their negations under available or specifiable evidence.

scoring_levels.0: Unfalsifiable in principle; no distinguishing criterion possible.
scoring_levels.1: Weak discriminability; criterion implicit or vague.
scoring_levels.2: Partial discriminability; criterion stated but not operationalized.
scoring_levels.3: Strong discriminability; criterion stated and operationalized.
scoring_levels.4: Full discriminability; falsifier specified with evidence path and domain.

R.description: Semantic redundancy. Degree to which the current state is semantically equivalent to one or more predecessors or contemporaneous states.
R.scoring_notes: INVERTED scale: 0 = no redundancy (best); 4 = full restatement (worst). Higher R degrades transition quality.

scoring_levels.0: No semantic overlap with predecessor or contemporaneous states.
scoring_levels.2: Moderate overlap; shared framing with distinct content.
scoring_levels.3: High overlap; effectively the same proposition in different phrasing.
scoring_levels.4: Full restatement; semantic equivalent of a predecessor claim.

diagnostic.description: S_n^diag = [B, A, U, K, X, V]_n — diagnostic dimensions. Independence among these is NOT presumed. Construct-separation failure must remain observable.

B.description: Boundary displacement. Degree to which the current state has shifted the claimed scope boundary relative to its predecessor.

A.description: Abstraction distance. Degree of distance between the current state's claims and the grounding evidence.

scoring_levels.2: Two inferential steps; each individually bounded.
scoring_levels.3: Three or more steps; some unbounded.
scoring_levels.4: Evidence-free abstraction; no path back to ground.

U.description: Uncertainty localization. Degree to which sources of uncertainty are explicitly identified and bounded.
U.scoring_notes: INVERTED scale: 0 = fully localized (best); 4 = uncertainty ignored (worst).

scoring_levels.0: All material uncertainty explicitly identified and bounded.

K.description: Consequentiality. Degree of downstream institutional or epistemic consequence carried by the current state's claims.

scoring_levels.1: Minor consequence; bounded to local inference.
scoring_levels.3: High consequence; affects interpretation of the whole trajectory.

X.description: Complexity burden. Degree of cognitive or computational complexity required to evaluate the current state.

scoring_levels.1: Low complexity; few propositions, each evaluable independently.
scoring_levels.2: Moderate complexity; requires holding multiple simultaneous claims.
scoring_levels.3: High complexity; nested dependencies or opaque structure.
scoring_levels.4: Excessive complexity; structurally resistant to evaluation.

V.description: Corrective revision. Degree to which the current state corrects, retracts, or revises a prior erroneous claim.

scoring_levels.0: No revision; continuation of prior state.
scoring_levels.2: Partial revision; one claim revised with acknowledgment.
scoring_levels.3: Substantial revision; multiple prior claims corrected.
scoring_levels.4: Full retraction; prior state superseded with preserved record.
